cities.d: (Finfinne) — capital of Ethiopia and one of the biggest shopping cities in Africa

x.around: Very few streets have names and those that do may not be named correctly on a map; use landmarks to navigate the city.

hidden.d: Pick up some dance lessons in salsa and bachata here so that you can impress the world later.
Walk from St. Mary church, the first church of Addis, and St Urael church and see the city from the top of the mountain.
Performances by traditional azmari minstrels.
Also known as the Menelik mausoleum, is located just south of the Menelik palace.
Green area in southern Addis, bisected by the Akaki stream.
Very interesting place and one of the many old churches in Addis Ababa. One can see old paintings by many Ethiopian celebrity artists.
Founded in 1955, the museum reportedly displays about 1100 species of African animals.
Built by the Derg regime of Mengistu Haile Mariam as its parliament hall, as of 2024 the known as the Office of the Prime Minister of Ethiopia.

x.intro: Addis Ababa (Amharic: አዲስ አበባ) is the capital and largest city of Ethiopia. With an estimated population of more than 6 million in 2026, it is growing very rapidly like many African cities. The city is an important center of diplomacy, and despite being a relatively young city, Addis is a good introduction to Ethiopia and its culture.

must.d: A poorly displayed but interesting museum. The most famous exhibit is the replica of Lucy, an early hominid. With Ethiopian civilization being one of the oldest in the world, the artefacts within the museum span thousands of…
It was built to commemorate the country's liberation from the Italians, and many victims killed by the Italians during occupation are buried here.

Built in 1896 to commemorate Ethiopia's victory over the Italians. The cathedral is an octagonal building. As you walk around it, you will notice people praying beside the walls, but it is unlikely that you will find an entrance.
The national library and archives of the country was opened by Emperor Haile Selassie in 1944, who also donated the first books.

About those who lost their lives in the time of the Derg. Opened in 2010 with an excellent, modern style of display. Visited in 2019 the building was in a fairly poor state with none of the lights seemingly working.

n.it: Museo memoriale dei martiri del Terrore rosso

must.d: Sometimes erroneously called Derg Monument, which Ethiopians find offensive because it is not a monument to honour the Derg regime. This massive statue monument was built in the 1980s.

Built as the Jubilee Palace to mark Emperor Haile Selassie's Silver Jubilee in 1955, it was the residence of the President of Ethiopia until, following an extensive renovation, it was opened to the public as the Palace Museum.
It's quite impressive, with its arcades and several minarets. Has been repainted at least twice in the 2010s and early 2020s.

next.d: and Sodere some 120 km to the southeast are popular weekend destinations for locals. The latter is famous for its hot springs. Adama is accessible by bus and train, from there minibuses go to Sodere.
200 km to the east by road, is a world heritage site where some of the earliest human remains have been found. It's also a good place to see hyenas, and another highlight is the Awash waterfalls.
is 550 km to the north, Ethiopia's third largest city and accessible by bus, car or plane. It's next to Lake Tana, and famous for churches and monasteries on islands in the lake as well as the Blue…
is an 11-hour train ride east along the new railway to Djibouti (you can fly here too). It's the only other chartered city in the country. A highlight here is Emperor Haile Selassie's Palace.
with the world heritage listed Paleolithic Melka Kunture excavation sites.
the "Stonehenge of Africa" is a world heritage listed ancient burial grounds, 90 km to the south. Accessible by car or bus.
162 km south is on the shore of an eponymous lake which is home to many species of birds. It's one of the Rift Valley lakes, and if you travel some 40 km further south, there are more lakes with…
as of May 2026, Abyssinian Luxury Coach goes directly to Nairobi. However, they seem to be not officially sanctioned by the government and have neither ticket office nor credit card payment system…

cities.d: (formerly also known as Nazret or Nazareth) — popular weekend destination near Addis

x.around: Street names and addresses are not discernibly marked (if, indeed, they are used at all). The Addis Ababa-Dire Dawa Road is the main thoroughfare through the town, and is pretty walkable by African standards, at least in the city center. Blue-and-white taxis use fixed routes along major streets, and cost less than one birr per person, per ride. These will pick up and let off other passengers along the route.
x.intro: Adama or Adaamaa, formerly known as Nazret, is a large city in central Ethiopia. It is a popular weekend destination for residents of Addis Ababa and hosts many governmental and non-governmental conferences.

cities.d: (Aksum) — home of ancient tombs and stelae fields, in the far north

x.around: Bajaj (blue, three-wheeler motorised rickshaws with 250cc two-stroke engines imported from India) charge tourists about 20 birr for short trips around town. For the Lioness of Gobodra and the Judith (Gudit) Stelae Field, instead of hiring one of the ultra-expensive tourist minibuses, you can catch a minibus going in the direction of Shire (there are many early in the morning) and ask them to drop you at the Lioness…

hidden.d: Of inferior quality in comparison to the Northern Stelae Field. On the other side of the road from the Dungur Palace.
A 20-min walk along the rough road heading northeast from the northern stelae field. Impressive foundations and tombs.

n.en: Tombs of Kings Kaleb and Gebre Mes'kel

hidden.d: near the St Mary of Zion complex, it is . This church is well worth inspecting as it has many colourful murals inside.

x.intro: Axum (አክሱም, also spelt Aksum) is a city of 56,000 in the Tigray region of Ethiopia, just south of Eritrea, with which it shares the language of Tigrinya.

must.d: Often just called Tsion Maryam, Ethiopian legend has it that this complex is the repository of the Ark of the Covenant (the subject of the controversial book The Sign and the Seal), which is said to have been stolen (with God's…

n.en: Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion
n.es: iglesia de Santa María de Sion
n.it: cattedrale di Nostra Signora Maria di Sion ad Axum

must.d: A well-preserved, 2-m-tall, thin tablet in Greek, Ge'ez and Latin discovered in the 1980s by a farmer, and praising God for his assistance in the conquest of land in what is now the Yemen.

The grand entrance steps and the foundations (topped with well dressed ruined walls up to 3 m high in places) of this palace near the Judith stelae field clearly indicate that this was the largest and most impressive palace in…

cities.d: monasteries on the islands of Lake Tana and the beautiful Blue Nile Falls nearby

x.around: Bajajs (three-wheel rick-shaws) are the most common form of transportation in the city. There are also blue minibuses, but few still exist as means to get around town. Bajajs are inexpensive and cost no more than two birr per line of road and 30-50 birr for a private charter.

hidden.d: Some of the world's oldest churches and monasteries are on islands in Lake Tana. There are lots of boat tours available to the monasteries. Entrance at each monastery is 100 birr as of 2016.
Bahir Dar grew around a Jesuit settlement, founded in the sixteenth or seventeenth century, from which time the Pedro Páez building dates.

n.en: Palace of Emperor Haile Selassie & Viewpoint over Bahir Dar/Blue Nile

hidden.d: A once spectacular sight that has been ruined by the building of a hydro-power dam. In rainy season (May to Sep) there is a decent flow but in the dry season the falls are pretty minimal and probably not worth suffering for 2.5-3…
Huge monument with waterfalls going to Blue Nile. Include a museum with pictures.

x.intro: Bahir Dar, also spelt Bahar Dar, on the southern shore of Lake Tana, the biggest lake in Ethiopia, is the third largest city in the nation, after Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa, with a population of half a million. It's the capital of the Amhara region, dominated by the Amhara people, the Ethiopia's second largest grouping; the Ethiopian official language is Amharic. Bahir Dar is a clean and well-maintained city by African standards.

next.d: to the north and the nearest big city, it has a complex of castles and palaces
to the west, its rock-hewn churches are a big attraction

x.safe: Like many other cities in Ethiopia, Bahir Dar is generally safe and free of violent crimes.

cities.d: the second largest city; in the east

x.around: The blue and white minibuses are in abundance in Dire Dawa, as are the small blue bajaji (auto rickshaws). These are easily hail-able from the street. Most Dire Dawa taxi drivers don't have a sense of time, if you tell your contracted taxi driver to pick you up or drop you of at a certain time, expect him to be late an hour or two.

hidden.d: A small palace built for former Emperor Haile Selassie. There have been talks to turn this into a museum, but no plans have materialized yet.

x.intro: Dire Dawa in eastern Ethiopia is the second-largest city in Ethiopia.
x.safe: Generally safe. However, you need to pay attention to your belongings. Your backpacks, camera and other shiny tourist items can attract pickpockets and con artists. Immigration of Somalis and a tension that may have created with locals has resulted in the city being heavily policed.

cities.d: some of East Africa's only castles

hidden.d: The remains of a royal fortified city that was founded by Fasilides (Fasil), emperor of Ethiopia from 1632 to 1667, and was the home of the emperors in the 17th and 18th centuries.

Across town from the Royal Enclosure, it once served as the bath for King Fasilides. Today it is used as a baptismal during Timket (18-21 January) where 30-40,000 people from all over the country gathers for swimming and mass.
The traffic in this busy intersection in the centre of town drives around a statue of the warrior emperor Tewodros II (ruler from 1855 to 1868).
On the eastern outskirts of town, it seems more like a fortress than a church at first glance. This is because the local churches were once vulnerable to attacks by the Sudanese.

x.intro: Gondar (also spelled Gonder) is a historic royal city of Ethiopia, in the northern Amhara region. It was the home of many emperors and princesses who ruled the country from the 12th century to the last decade of the 20th century, including Suseneos, Fasiledes, Empress Mentwab, Iyasu I, Tewodros II and Empress Taitu. Leading the list of its attractions is Fasil Ghebbi (the Royal Enclosure), containing several castles and palaces from the 17th and 18th centuries.

next.d: to the south

x.safe: There is the occasional scam where a tourist prepays a guide for a Simien Mountain trip and the guide is never seen again. Do not pay cash to guides unless they have a shopfront or you have contacted them after receiving a recommendation from a reliable source!

cities.d: ancient walled city near Dire Dawa

x.around: Auto rickshaws ("bajaji" in Ethiopia) are readily available. Flag one down pretty much anywhere. There is no need to take them around the Jugol as it is very walkable.

hidden.d: Located in a mansion where Haile Selassie lived as a child. Better to have a guide for this one to explain the dusty artifacts.
A beautiful Ethiopian Orthodox cathedral on the Feres Magala square.
One of two churches in the Jugol. Has an impressive carved wood door.
Watch hyenas and then feed them yourself with rotten meat. Every bajaj and taxi driver knows the location, but you can walk there from the old city.

Purchase meat from the Gidir Magala butcher shops and then feed the black kites (birds of prey) waiting patiently above you. Or you can sit around and see if they get lucky enough to snatch someone else's meat.

Displays artifacts of the region. Its gate is locked as of 2025, although the signs are still up and it appears well maintained. Across the street are mansions that belonged to Haile Selassie's family.
A domed shrine for the 16th-century Emir of Harar.
A mansion that once housed the renowned French poet Arthur Rimbaud now converted to a museum.

x.intro: Harar (sometimes spelled Harrar or Harer) is an ancient city in eastern Ethiopia. Harar Jugol, the old walled city is a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is considered the fourth holiest city of Islam by Sunni Muslims (after Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem), with 82 mosques, three of which date from the 10th century, and 102 shrines.

must.d: At the centre of the Jugol. Only Muslims may enter.

next.d: Ethiopia's hot and dusty second-largest city.
and then onward to Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland (you'll need a Somaliland visa).
there are buses leaving daily early morning (04:30 or 05:00). Buy your ticket a few days in advance. There are a few companies and most of the offices are located at Charleville Ave, near Bank of…

cities.d: is a town in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia. Home to 11 astonishing rock-hewn churches

x.around: You may lose a few kilos walking up and down the streets (some cobbled, some dirt). You can rent bajajis/tuktuks or minibuses to drive you around town for about 25 birr per person (minimum 50 birr). Unlike bigger towns and cities in Ethiopia, no blue and white minibuses regularly run through Lalibela.
x.intro: Lalibela is a rural town of 15,000 people in a stunning setting at an elevation of 2,600 m (8,500 ft) in the midst of the Lasta mountains in the eastern highlands of Northern Ethiopia. Its unique and remarkable monolithic churches hewn from living rock, most built more than 900 years ago, are one of Ethiopia's leading attractions and were declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1978.

next.d: to the west
to the north

cities.d: a town in the Tigrayan Highlands in the north

x.intro: Mekele is in the Tigrayan Highlands in Ethiopia. It is the capital of the Tigray region and has a population of 200,000.

next.d: to the north, in an area with many rock-hewn churches
and nearby Yeha with its ancient temple, further north than Hawzien

intro: Ethiopia is Africa's third-most populous country (after Nigeria and Egypt), oldest independent country and one of only two never colonised by a European power, save for a short Italian occupation in the 1930s and 1940s.

x.intro: Abijatta-Shalla Lakes National Park is in the southern Oromia region of Ethiopia, about 200 km south of the capital of Addis Ababa.

n.it: parco nazionale delle montagne di Bale

x.around: The park is reasonably drivable. You can cross the Sanetti Plateau on Africa's highest all-weather road.
x.intro: Bale Mountains National Park is in Southern Ethiopia. In 2023 the park was listed as a .

x.around: Large areas of the park need a good 4×4 with high chassis, particularly to visit the northern part including the Hot Springs, where the dirt road is damaged. A standard car can access the southern area south of national highway number 4.

hidden.d: Waterfalls are more impressive during or just after the rainy season. Sometimes, olive baboons cross the river on the rocks at the top of the waterfalls and are visible from the lodge.
Viewpoint on the Awash River gorges and one of its tributaries.

n.en: Viewpoint on the Awash River gorges

x.intro: Awash National Park is in Ethiopia. The Lower Valley of the Awash, a site where some of the earliest human remains have been found, was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1980.

next.d: south of Addis Ababa, likewise an archaeological site with remains of hominid life from almost two million years before present.
a 1-hour detour on the way back to Addis Ababa, to see the natural hot springs and the spa, near Awash River. 25 km south of Adama on national highway 8.

x.intro: Mago National Park is in south-western Ethiopia, towards the border with South Sudan and Kenya. It is east of the Omo River, and stretches south towards the Chew Bahir basin. Omo National Park is on the western side of the Omo River.

must.d: Tributary of the Mago River. Serves as a vital perennial water source and is a scenic spot for birdwatching and wildlife within gallery forests and surrounding acacia woodlands.

x.intro: Omo National Park is in south-western Ethiopia, towards the border with South Sudan and Kenya, and west of the Omo River.

x.around: A road runs from Debark through the park and accesses some of the campsites and villages. 4x4s and lorries go through Sankaber, Geech and Chenek, but tourists are prohibited from using them and most visitors use mountain hiking paths to get around. As a tourist, the only way into the park are to hire a 4x4, walk or go with a tour company.
x.intro: Simien National Park, also known as Simien Mountains National Park], is in the Amhara region in northern Ethiopia. It was one of the first sites added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1978. It features spectacular scenery viewed from its peaks and escarpments and fascinating gelada monkeys and other wildlife. The park headquarters are outside the park in Debark, the nearest town, on the main road between Gondar (to the south) and Shire and Axum (to the north).

next.d: and its royal castles to the south. Minibuses leave from the bus station and cost 75 birr. They also charge 25 birr/50 birr for small/big luggage but it is unsure if this is legitimate, i.e.
with its stelae and other historic structures to the north

other.d: spa town due to hot springs (filwoha)

x.intro: Sodere is a spa town (population 1,900) in Ethiopia that has natural hot springs. It is a weekend get-away place for people from Addis Ababa.

x.around: You can walk most of the town. To get up the hill to the west (e.g. to the cultural village), take a bejaj (tuk tuk).
x.intro: Konso is a small town in Southern Ethiopia. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2011.

northeast
